name: POST /api/leadflow/offers/:id/activate - exactly one quotable version
description:
Makes an approved version the one reps quote (92ce5959-0e5c-4ce8-be7a-02cc870b2120#AC1). SUPERSEDING THE PREVIOUS VERSION IS PART OF ACTIVATION, in the same request: two active versions would mean two reps quoting different terms and both believing they were current, and a partial unique index refuses the second one outright rather than trusting the handler to remember.

ACTIVATION WITHOUT THE FULL ROUTE IS A 409, NOT A 400 (92ce5959-0e5c-4ce8-be7a-02cc870b2120#AC2). The request is well formed and the version is real; the world is simply not in a state where activation is permitted, and the refusal names who is still outstanding. A database CHECK enforces the same rule, so an unapproved sheet cannot be activated by any writer - putting unreviewed terms in front of a buyer is the harm.

QA: depends on the draft and its approvals, both read from the cache.

testCases.name: An approved version becomes active and supersedes the previous one
NEGATIVE: no version with that id
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all
NEGATIVE: a bearer token that does not verify

errorCases.message: No offer version with that id
errorCases.when: the offer version id does not exist.

errorCases.message: This version is still awaiting legal and finance. Activating an unapproved sheet would put unreviewed terms in front of a buyer.
errorCases.when: any party on the approval route has not signed off. The request is well formed; the world is not in a state where activation is permitted.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer.

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify.
